body:
>       Then, Wattsi, uses this block like normal, but in the final output pass, removes the entire `<div data-wattsi-dependencies>` so that it doesn't show up in the final output.

I would be happy to implement that in Wattsi — if in fact there ends up being agreement to drop the section

>     * Currently by clicking on a term in the dependencies section you can see all the places it's referenced. We'd lose that.

It’s imaginable that we wouldn’t need to lose that completely. At least we wouldn’t need to lose the part where when you click on an *instance* of a term, you can still end up getting the dfn popop — it’s just that after that click, we’d need to make a way to invoke the popup without clicking on a term. Or actually, maybe we could use some scripting to inject the term into the DOM somewhere after you click on a instance of the term?

Just kind of thinking out loud — but anyway it seems not impossible…

And I think that if we could make the UX/UI work for that, then there’s very little downside in making this change.

The only downside would then be that a reader couldn’t browse through the list of dependency/external terms and click on them to start things off. But is that the normal use case anyway? At least personally, I think the way I usually initiate the dfn popups anyway is by first clicking on an instance of a term, not the term itself.

>     * Other specs have a (autogenerated) "terms defined by reference" section. I'm proposing that we lose ours. Is that OK?

It seems OK to me — because, I don’t know if the use case of browsing through the "terms defined by reference" section is a very typical use case at all. For me it’s certainly not at least.
I use "terms defined by reference" occasionally to spot errors or find a term by its canonical spelling. Overall though this seems okay.
